title: Optimization of multistate STIRAP by pulse shaping
authors: Julian K. Dimitrov, Nikolay V. Vitanov
abstract: We propose a pulse-shaping method for improving population transfer in multistate stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) with nearest-neighbour couplings only. The method extends the quasiparallel-eigenenergy approach, previously used for two- and three-state systems, to multistate chains without introducing additional shortcut fields. The pump and Stokes fields are shaped so that the eigenenergies closest to the dark state remain nearly parallel to it during the central part of the interaction, where nonadiabatic transitions are most likely to occur. We derive analytic prescriptions for the required pulse shapes and apply them to five-, seven-, and nine-state chains formed by magnetic sublevels of degenerate manifolds with angular momenta $J_g\rightarrow J_e=J_g$ and $J_g\rightarrow J_e=J_g-1$ driven by a pair of right- and left-circularly polarized pulses. Numerical simulations show that the optimized pulses can reduce the population transfer error by several orders of magnitude compared to standard Gaussian pulses. The same shapes also improve robustness against variations of the peak Rabi frequency, the single-photon detuning, and the multiphoton detuning. The comparison between the two angular-momentum families shows that the $J_g\rightarrow J_g$ chains are generally more favourable, because their Clebsch-Gordan coefficients keep the relevant bright-state gap larger in the region where the dark state changes most rapidly. Finally, simulations with spontaneous emission show that the optimized resonant pulses remain advantageous in the lossy regime as well.
summary: This paper introduces a sophisticated pulse-shaping technique to enhance population transfer fidelity in complex multistate STIRAP systems. By tailoring the driving laser fields based on keeping system eigenenergies parallel to the dark state, the authors achieve error reductions of several orders of magnitude over standard pulses. This method proves highly effective for controlling quantum transitions in atomic ensembles and remains robust even when accounting for environmental decoherence.
main_problem: The primary goal is improving population transfer efficiency in multistate Stimulated Raman Adiabatic Passage (STIRAP) protocols.
main_result: Optimized pulse shaping can reduce the population transfer error by several orders of magnitude compared to standard Gaussian pulses, and this improvement remains robust against parameter variations and spontaneous emission.
method: The authors propose a novel pulse-shaping method extending the quasiparallel-eigenenergy approach. This involves analytically designing pump and Stokes field shapes to keep relevant eigenenergies nearly parallel to the dark state during critical interaction periods.
model_or_system: The system models multistate STIRAP chains, specifically using magnetic sublevels of degenerate angular momenta ($J_g 	o J_e$). The dynamics are governed by time-dependent Hamiltonian evolution under coupling from right- and left-circularly polarized pulses.
key_observables: Population transfer error (fidelity), instantaneous eigenenergies ($\eta$), and the dark-bright energy gap separation.
important_parameters: Pulse shapes, Rabi frequencies ($\Omega_p, \Omega_s$), single-photon detuning ($\Delta$), multiphoton detuning ($\delta$), and the number of states in the chain (odd numbers $N=2n+1$).
main_assumptions: The method is restricted to odd-numbered state chains because these generically possess a zero-eigenvalue dark state. The approach avoids introducing auxiliary shortcut fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three-state $\Lambda$ configuration, show optimized pulse shapes for various multi-state systems, and present 2D maps comparing population transfer error versus parameter variations (e.g., Gaussian vs. optimized pulses).
paper_structure: The paper builds from the basic three-state STIRAP model to generalize the concept of quasiparallel eigenenergies to arbitrary odd-numbered state chains, deriving analytic pulse prescriptions and validating them through extensive numerical simulations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses high-fidelity quantum control in open quantum systems by optimizing external driving fields. The extension of adiabatic passage techniques to complex, multi-level atomic structures is highly relevant for quantum memory and quantum simulation using trapped atoms or superconducting circuits.
